directAnswer: Pope Urban III was Uberto Crivelli, archbishop of Milan, who reigned from November 1185 to October 1187. Elected at Verona, he spent his short pontificate in a bitter dispute with Emperor Frederick Barbarossa and his son Henry VI, and died at Ferrara as news of the crusader defeat at Hattin was reaching Europe.

paras: Uberto was born at Cuggiono, near Milan, into the Crivelli family. He was made a cardinal and became archbishop of Milan in 1185. Elected pope at Verona on November 25, 1185, the day Lucius III died, he kept the archbishopric of Milan, a city that had suffered greatly at Frederick Barbarossa's hands, which helps explain his firm stance toward the emperor.

sections.h2: Quarrels With Frederick and Henry VI
paras: In January 1186 Frederick's son Henry married Constance, heiress of the Kingdom of Sicily, in Milan, a union that threatened to surround the Papal States with Hohenstaufen power. Urban refused to crown Henry as co-emperor. He also consecrated Folmar as archbishop of Trier against the emperor's wishes, and Henry's troops responded by occupying parts of the Papal States. German bishops largely sided with the emperor.

Urban was preparing to excommunicate Frederick when he died at Ferrara on October 20, 1187. Some chroniclers say grief over the defeat of the crusader army at Hattin in July 1187 hastened his death, though that account cannot be verified. He was buried in Ferrara Cathedral.

keyFacts: Personal name: Uberto Crivelli, archbishop of Milan
Refused to crown Henry VI as co-emperor
Died at Ferrara and buried in its cathedral

faqs.question: Why did Urban III clash with Frederick Barbarossa?
faqs.answer: He resisted the marriage alliance linking the Hohenstaufen to Sicily, refused to crown Henry VI as co-emperor, and consecrated an archbishop of Trier the emperor opposed.

faqs.question: Did Urban III die of grief over Hattin?
faqs.answer: Some medieval chroniclers say so, but it cannot be confirmed. He died at Ferrara in October 1187, a few months after the battle.
